text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- A fresh wave of tourists arrives on the Croatian coast and preliminary assessments show the 1997 season will be the best since Croatia gained its independence.

- Odds are slim on the possible meeting of Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic and his Yugoslav counterpart Milan Milutinovic before the end of July. The reason for this is the still unprepared documents that the two should sign.
- Damage assessment teams are to enter the 'Baranja triangle' today and start their inspection of some 500 homes in the area.
- The Croatian political scene will not become bi-polarised due to the hard patch that HSLS and the HSS are going through, says SDP leader Ivica Racan in an interview.
- Foreign visitors are making illegal money on the Croatian coast by renting out yachts, bicycles and boats.
- The Zagreb HSLS party has set eight conditions that the ruling HDZ party has to meet in order for the agreement on power-sharing in the city authorities to come to fruition.
- The Dubrovnik region is expecting to have one million overnight stays by the end of summer. At the moment some 2,500 are staying in the city.
- One of the founders of the Serb National Council (SNV) in Croatia Milorad Pupovac believes the organisaton will solve the status of Serbs in Craotia.
- Viktor Lenac repair docks to sign an agreement for listing on the Zagreb Stock Exchange.
VECERNJI LIST

- INA oil company and its Italian partner Agip wind down preparations for the exploration of the 2,400 square metre Aiza-Laura gas field in the northern Adriatic in the hope of finding sufficient gas reserves.
- Croatian insignia to be introduced today on the Croatian-Yugoslav border crossing near Ilok.
- Some 18,592 residents of Zagreb are benefactors of the social welfare system.
- Two drug addicts use a fire extinguisher to brutally kill a taxi driver, in Velika Gorica near Zagreb, for his money.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- The new social welfare law that will be introduced in January 1998 envisages that all those able to work will no longer receive financial assistance.
- Austrians will be allowed to import only 25 cigarettes or five cigars when returning home from countries not belonging to the European Union as of July 1.
- Croatian citizens to be granted favourable loans even before the year's end, says Bank Austria Croatia president Anton Knett in an interview. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
